movement_abstract: 【伊拉克库尔德斯坦埃尔比勒报道】2026 年 8 月 26 日，伊朗武装部队发言人阿博尔法兹尔·谢卡奇准将在访问德法通讯社时发表言论，明确威胁在境外工作的波斯语媒体记者。谢卡奇点名伊朗国际电视台、BBC 波斯语频道、Manoto 和自由电台，指控这些机构与以色列摩萨德及美国中央情报局直接关联，接受其行动指令。他宣称这些媒体员工是“犹太复国主义”和“美国”的士兵，并非新闻机构，因此可能被列入军事目标库。此举标志着伊朗对境外波斯语媒体威胁升级，将新闻工作直接等同于参战行为。伊朗当局长期将境外波斯语广播视为心理战和国家安全威胁，曾于 2017 年冻结 152 名 BBC 波斯语员工资产。今年 6 月伊朗与以色列冲突后，伊朗通过新立法，本月内已有 16 名记者被拘，摄影记者瓦尔达·莫艾里因向被指敌对的媒体提供采访和照片，被判处 15 年监禁。西方政府及人权组织批评此类逮捕具有政治动机，但德黑兰予以否认。

content: The Trump administration has announced unspecified plans to further tighten sanctions on Iran, threatening other countries, including China, in the process. We speak to sanctions expert Nicholas Mulder about what he calls the “rhetorical” and “psychological warfare” of the announcement. For Iran, says Mulder, the announcement was not “really materially all that meaningful. And to the extent that they are, they hurt ordinary Iranians and not the government.” The impact on the U.S. relationship with China, however, could be much greater. If the U.S. does place secondary sanctions on Iran’s trading partners, the “U.S.-China trade truce might be unraveling,” warns Mulder. “The space for maneuver that the U.S. has in using these tools of very coercive economic statecraft has narrowed.” The Trump administration has outlined plans to tighten sanctions on Iran, warning that businesses, banks and other nations could lose access to the U.S. financial system if they continue doing business with Tehran. On Monday, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent announced “Operation Economic Outcast,” which includes secondary sanctions on trade related to Iran’s oil, shipping, cryptocurrency, gold and aviation industries. Bessent said countries have a defined timeline to sever ties with Iran, but provided no details on which countries would be targeted, or when. After Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent finished his remarks, he took questions from reporters. Iran has threatened to retaliate against the U.S. in a, quote, “seismic” manner. Iranian officials have said that any country supporting the new U.S. economic restrictions would be considered an enemy. This is Iran’s economy minister, Ali Madanizadeh. To talk more about the U.S. economic war against Iran, we are joined now by Nicholas Mulder. He’s an associate professor of history at Cornell University and a specialist in sanctions. He’s the author of . Nicholas Mulder, welcome to Your response to this announcement yesterday? There’s not a lot of details on enforcement. And what does this mean for China? China is Iran’s largest economic trading partner, buys over 80% of its oil, and President Trump is set to meet with the Chinese premier next month. Yeah. Thank you for having me. I think that this announcement really shows that the United States is trying to increase the pressure on Iran, but is primarily doing so at the moment by rhetorical means and a kind of psychological warfare. Of course, Iran has been under a naval blockade imposed by the United States since June. The Iranian economy is feeling the pressure of that. And the announcement yesterday was very short, as you mentioned, on details. There was a hint that a major global financial institution might be designated under the sanctions soon, but that, too, was left very vague. It could have been a veiled threat towards China. It could have been a sort of general attempt to create a chilling effect around these transactions. The reality is that at this point there are relatively few sanctions that the United States can take that directly affect Iran. There were some things thrown in to the announcement and to the designations by the Treasury, such as a ban on all remaining remittances to Iran, a ban on remaining academic and sports exchanges. But these really just seem gratuitous ways to try and show that this is an attempt to isolate Iran even further. They weren’t really materially all that meaningful. And to the extent that they are, they hurt ordinary Iranians and not the government. The real way that the U.S. is going to try and enforce these sanctions is by putting pressure on third countries trading with Iran, and I think that’s where it’s going to be an open question whether these sanctions will be as forceful as Bessent wants them to be. The big trading partner, as you already mentioned, is China, but we’re also talking about Pakistan, Turkey, India and a number of other countries that trade a lot with Iran and, you know, that see that they have every right to, that these are, at the end of the day, just American sanctions — they’re not international legal measures. And these countries claim, and for themselves, the right to sovereign — make sovereign decisions about who they can trade with and who they cannot. The Chinese have already announced that they’re going to not just ignore them, but even make sure that countries and companies within China will not comply with them. And recently Chinese courts have also begun to put sanctions on companies that complied with American sanctions. So, I think that this is no longer an empty counterthreat, either. And the stakes are pretty high when it comes to the relationship with China, because, of course, the United States is in a very fragile truce, if you could still call it that, on the trade war. So, any excessive pressure on China, I think, is going to be very likely to reopen that. And there’s already been a tit-for-tat spate of measures in the last few weeks dealing with tariffs about overcapacity, restrictions on drone exports and imports, that suggests that this U.S.-China trade truce might be unraveling. And I think this Iran sanctions episode is really likely to further unravel that if the U.S. goes through with secondary sanctions enforcement. And, Professor Mulder, about this issue of potential sanctions on large financial institutions, most people are not aware that about four of the 10 largest banks in the world are headquartered — are Chinese banks headquartered in China. If you include , which is in Hong Kong, it’s half of the largest financial institutions of the world have direct ties with China. So, what would be the impact of any attempt to sanction, for instance, a major Chinese bank or institution? So, initially, it would depend on what kind of sanctions are placed on that bank, whether this is blocking them from participation in dollar markets or whether it’s done through a full blocking order. There’s a different range of sanctions that the U.S. could take. The impact for the Chinese would be that they would have difficulty immediately accessing the U.S. financial system, but that cuts both ways. They have a lot of reserves saved up. And it would almost automatically also have a major effect on Asian financial markets. These Chinese banks hold large amounts of reserves in Hong Kong, but also in Singapore and other markets, and that will cause liquidity issues there. So, I think that this is something that can’t really be sized up that quickly. Like you mentioned, the the largest bank, Industrial and Commercial Bank of China,, it’s the the single largest financial institution by assets, and so we’re dealing really with hundreds of billions of dollars in assets. I very much doubt that the American government, at this particular moment, would choose to put sanctions on China’s largest bank, given that the Chinese have also shown that they will immediately retaliate with rare earth export controls. They could retaliate by taking measures against all kinds of U.S. foreign investments in China. There is still, of course, a significant degree of American capital in China. So, they could counter-freeze, and that could very quickly escalate. And at this moment, of course, we should sketch the broader picture here, which is that the United States has entered a period where its own sovereign debt, the Treasury market, is no longer as stable as it once was. The rates are very high. And Bessent has spent the last two weeks desperately trying to talk down the Treasury yields, trying to make sure that American government debt remains an attractive asset class to invest in. But bigger question marks have really emerged over that. So, if he puts really aggressive sanctions on Iran, it will very quickly tend to backfire against American economic conditions. And there’s two ways. One of them could be through the China channel. The other one could be by further removing oil from global markets. If there is a significant oil importer — say, India — that is immediately and quickly cut off by American secondary sanctions, then what you might see is an immediate pass-through into U.S. inflation, expectations that interest rates are going to go up. We’re coming up against the Federal Reserve meeting soon, in the coming week, and an announcement by Kevin Warsh at the Jackson Hole symposium about interest rates, and that is certain to feed into the Treasury market immediately, and that would be exactly the opposite of what Bessent is trying to achieve. So, I see that announcement of him yesterday and the way that he handled the questions as of a piece with his broader attempt to talk the bond market into submission, or at least a kind of quietude, to try and get the bond vigilantes off the back of the American Treasury. The issue is, of course, here that, you know, the bond market, as well as other countries, get a vote, as well, and the space for maneuver that the U.S. has in using these tools of very coercive economic statecraft has narrowed. And I’m wondering also, the issue of the United Arab Emirates. Just before Bessent’s announcement, the announced that it was ending trade relations with Iran. Can you talk about the significance of this? And in fact, while all these hostilities have been going on, trade across the Persian Gulf between the and Iran has continued for all of these months. Yes, so, the has always been an important trading partner for Iran. There’s also a very large Iranian diasporic community there and people who move back and forth between Iran and the Emirates. And it has long been a hub for a lot of commercial companies, but that also includes the , Iranian state companies, as well as private entities. So, that’s long been the case. It’s also been the case that the Emirates, of course, was a major target of the initial Italian — sorry, Iranian retaliation against the American and Israeli attack after February. But then, in the last six to eight weeks, Iranian attacks on the Emirates really fell off dramatically, and there’s been quite plausible speculation that this was because there was an arrangement that was reached between the Emirates and the Iranian government, and a certain modicum of trade was reallowed in exchange, perhaps, also for Emirati payments or unfreezing of frozen Iranian assets there. Now, if the Trump administration, as the Emiratis appear to signal, has now reimposed these sanctions, and the Emiratis at least want to suggest that they are complying, two things can be happening: Either they have reimposed this, these restrictions, in which case they would invite pretty prompt Iranian retaliation, or they’re trying to take action against a certain big headline set of commercial activities, while allowing, under the surface, some of it to continue. I think one should not underestimate the fact that the Gulf countries have been forced in recent months to really recalibrate their relationships, both to the United States but also to China and to a number of other countries. And they realize that the United States is less able to protect them, that American actions against Iran expose them to retaliation, that that means both increased assertiveness on their own part militarily and geopolitically, but also developing their own relations with regional powers. And that includes, eventually, I think, some kind of with Iran. So, there’s definitely been, I think, a lot of signaling, but we cannot take the Emirati announcement completely at face value, either. The proof will have to be in analyzing commercial data and trade data in the months to come, and only in time can we tell if this is really what’s happening. Nicholas Mulder, how is this playing out in Iran? I mean, yesterday, the Iranian rial dropped to a record low of nearly 2 million to the dollar. But Iranian government officials continue to dismiss the Trump administration sanctions announcement. Is there a disconnect between the political defiance we’re seeing from the Iranian government and the actual impact of the sanctions on the ground? Well, the sanctions have definitely had an impact, and the U.S. naval blockade, to be more specific, more still, since the beginning of June. For ordinary Iranians, of course, this war, which did not spare them in the least, has been horrific. On top of that, there’s major reconstruction costs that are now very difficult to finance because of Iran’s relative isolation. And what exports had been getting out of Iran, in the form of oil and other exports, now have also dropped off. So, Iran is no longer as free to trade as it wants. There are a number of overland routes that have been activated with neighboring countries, but those have a much reduced volume in terms of what they can sustain. And I do think you’re right to suggest that the Iranian government — certainly, the people that now seem to be having the most influence over decision-making, a number of and military figures — believe that this economic blockade shows that the Americans are out of military options, and that actually they interpret this as a sign of American weakness. So, they’re not afraid to up the ante further and to threaten retaliation. And they seem also quite capable of carrying it out, if they so choose. The question is: Whose negotiating position is going to strengthen further by that kind of escalation? Will time be on the side of the Trump administration, or is the Trump administration actually itself racing against the economic clock with, like I said, rising inflation in the U.S., a deteriorating bond market, midterms coming up? In Iran, the government seems determined to ride this out, even if it means that the population will continue to suffer further in the near term. So, yeah, that’s how I see the lay of the land as it stands right now. Nicholas Mulder is an associate professor of history at Cornell University and a specialist in sanctions, is the author of . Thank you so much for joining us. Coming up, we look at how local officials in Illinois are collaborating with federal immigration agents despite a state law barring the practice. Stay with us. [break] “El Hielo/ ,” by La Santa Cecilia in our studio.
title: U.S. Threatens New Economic War on Iran by Targeting China & Tehran’s Other Top Trading Partners

movement_abstract: 特朗普政府宣布启动'经济孤立行动'，计划进一步收紧对伊朗的制裁，威胁切断与伊朗在石油、航运、加密货币、黄金及航空领域有业务往来的国家、企业及银行进入美国金融系统的渠道。美国财政部长斯科特·贝森特表示，相关国家需在限定时间内切断与伊朗联系，但未公布具体目标国及时间表。伊朗方面威胁将采取'地震式'报复，并将支持新制裁的国家视为敌人。制裁专家尼古拉斯·穆尔德分析指出，该公告缺乏具体执行细节，实质为'修辞性'和'心理战'手段，对伊朗政府实质性影响有限，主要伤害普通民众。然而，若美国对伊朗贸易伙伴实施二级制裁，将严重冲击中美贸易休战局面。中国作为伊朗最大贸易伙伴，进口其超80%石油，已明确表示不遵守美国制裁，并可能通过稀土出口管制等措施反制。穆尔德警告，针对中国大型金融机构的制裁可能引发亚洲金融市场流动性危机及通胀反弹，反噬美国经济。此外，阿联酋虽宣布终止与伊朗贸易，但实际执行情况存疑，海湾国家正重新调整与美、中及地区大国的关系。伊朗里亚尔兑美元汇率跌至近200万的历史低点，但伊朗政府视美国封锁为军事选项耗尽的软弱表现，意图通过升级对抗维持谈判地位。

content: Kashmiri Pandit employees working in the Valley have sought immediate security measures from the Jammu and Kashmir administration after a fresh threat poster circulated on social media allegedly under the banner of a shadow outfit calling itself the United Liberation Council (ULC). The All PM Package Employees Forum Kashmir has submitted a representation to the Chief Secretary of Jammu and Kashmir, seeking urgent security enhancements for migrant Kashmiri Pandit employees amid a growing cyber threat environment. The representation refers to a poster dated August 23, 2026, which, unlike generic threat messages, allegedly contains sensitive personal information of individual employees. The details reportedly include full names, residential addresses and vehicle registration numbers, raising concerns over how such information may have been obtained and circulated. Security agencies are yet to establish the authenticity and provenance of the document. However, the forum has argued that the appearance of targeted lists itself has created considerable anxiety among employees and their families. The concerns are particularly acute among Kashmiri Pandit employees because of the community’s history of targeted attacks in the Valley. Previous killings of minority employees and civilians have left many families apprehensive about threats that identify individuals by name or location. The forum has called for an immediate investigation into the origin of the poster and a comprehensive review of security arrangements at places of posting, residential quarters and along daily transit routes. It has also sought targeted security cover and clearly defined safety protocols for employees whose addresses, vehicle details or other personal records have appeared in the alleged threat material. According to top Indian intelligence sources, agencies are examining the ULC’s emergence and its possible links to established Pakistan-backed terror networks, including Lashkar-e-Taiba (LeT). Intelligence assessments suggest that such shadow outfits can be used to issue threats and conduct psychological operations while providing established terror handlers with a layer of deniability. Investigators are also examining whether any local administrative databases or other sources of personal information may have been compromised or accessed to obtain precise residential addresses, vehicle details and other identifying information. Security officials are increasingly viewing such digital campaigns as a form of low-cost psychological warfare. Beyond threatening individuals, the objective could be to generate fear among minority employees, disrupt government rehabilitation and employment initiatives, and pressure vulnerable groups into withdrawing from postings in the Valley. For Kashmiri Pandit employees, the latest episode has therefore revived an old fear in a new form: threats that travel through social media but can have very real consequences on the ground.
title: Kashmiri Pandit Employees In Valley Seek Urgent Security After Threat Poster Leaks Personal Details

movement_abstract: 【印度情报部门8月25日报道】2026年8月23日，印控克什米尔地区出现一张疑似由名为‘联合解放委员会’（ULC）的地下组织发布的威胁海报，导致当地工作的克什米尔教派（Kashmiri Pandit）员工面临安全危机。该海报包含多名员工的姓名、家庭住址及车辆注册号码等敏感个人信息。‘全PM包员工论坛克什米尔分会’已向查谟和克什米尔首席秘书提交请愿书，要求立即加强安保措施。安全机构正在核实文件真实性，并调查信息泄露源头，怀疑当地行政数据库可能遭入侵。印度情报部门评估认为，ULC可能与巴基斯坦支持的‘虔诚军’（LeT）等恐怖网络存在关联，此类组织常被用于实施心理战以制造恐慌。安全官员指出，此类低成本数字行动旨在恐吓少数族裔员工，破坏政府安置计划，迫使相关人员撤离。鉴于该社区历史上曾遭受针对性袭击，此次事件引发强烈焦虑，论坛呼吁对受威胁员工实施针对性安保覆盖并审查通勤路线安全。

content: Security and intelligence agencies in Jammu and Kashmir have raised alarms over a renewed wave of intimidation directed at minority Kashmiri Hindu families and government employees living in the region. The emergence of purported online threat letters and notices—which explicitly publish sensitive personal data, residential addresses, and contact numbers—has been classified by security experts as a calculated tactic of psychological warfare. The circulation of these circulars, reportedly attributed to shadow groups and fringe outfits operating in the Valley, marks an escalation from generic threats to targeted intimidation. By singling out specific individuals and government personnel, the campaign seeks to exploit personal vulnerabilities and foster an atmosphere of panic. Intelligence assessments indicate that the primary objective of publishing such details is not merely physical confrontation, but psychological destabilization—aiming to resurrect deep-seated anxieties and fracture the fragile sense of normalcy among minority communities. In response to the growing unease, community forums and employee associations have urgently appealed to the administration for heightened safety protocols and comprehensive threat evaluations. Law enforcement and administrative bodies have initiated rigorous digital audits to track the origin of these notices, verify their authenticity, and assess potential data leaks. Security grids across sensitive districts have been reinforced, with authorities emphasizing a zero-tolerance approach toward elements attempting to disrupt communal harmony and terrorize civilians through digital propaganda.
title: Psychological Warfare in the Valley: Fresh Threats Target Kashmiri Hindu Families - idrw.org

movement_abstract: 印控查谟和克什米尔地区安全与情报机构发出警报，指出针对当地少数族裔克什米尔印度教家庭及政府雇员的恐吓活动出现新一轮升级。安全专家将此类行为定性为精心策划的心理战战术，其核心特征是发布包含敏感个人数据、家庭住址及联系方式的在线威胁信件。情报评估显示，这些通告据称由山谷地区活动的影子团体及边缘组织发布，标志着威胁手段从泛化恐吓转向针对特定个人的精准施压。该行动旨在利用个人脆弱性制造恐慌氛围，其首要目标并非直接引发肢体冲突，而是通过心理 destabilization 手段重燃少数族裔深层焦虑，破坏当地脆弱的正常生活秩序。面对日益加剧的不安情绪，社区论坛及员工协会已紧急呼吁行政当局加强安全协议并开展全面威胁评估。执法与行政机构随即启动严格的数字审计程序，以追踪通告源头、核实真实性并评估潜在数据泄露风险。当局已在敏感地区强化安全网格部署，并强调对试图通过数字宣传破坏社区和谐、恐吓平民的行为采取零容忍态度。

content: Republican or Democrat, I don't necessarily like writing about politicians' kids, especially those who don't choose to put themselves out there. As we all know, 20-year-old Barron Trump lives a fairly private life, especially compared to his parents and siblings. But the Iranian regime is not so kind. As a matter of fact, what it did recently is some of the worst propaganda I've seen in a while. From what I understand, Iranian state TV (Channel 3) played a three-minute video called "Where to kill Barron Trump." That alone should give you an idea of just how gruesome it was. And as if that wasn't bad enough, it also allegedly offered a $10 million reward for his death. I don't think that's confirmed in the video, but it's being widely reported. I should also note that the original video did not appear anywhere online in an official capacity, so we're stuck with what's being passed around on social media. I saw some of the AI-generated video on anti-regime London-based journalist Niyak Ghorbani's X account, and it has English subtitles, so I'm going by those since I do not speak the language. But it starts out claiming that a girl was able to get past the Secret Service protocols and have a private meeting with Barron, and she apparently handed the regime or whoever made the video the information about his day-to-day life. It then goes on to explain where and how Barron spends his days in New York and Washington, D.C., both at home and at school, as well as how he gets around in a convoy of Secret Service vehicles. It even talks about the classes he takes, how his "bodyguards" are always around and he's never alone, and how those Secret Service members ditch their suits and dress casually like students to blend in with his classmates. It also shows some NYU dorm rooms. But then it claims there's a loophole in Barron's, whom the video calls "reclusive," online presence. It says he does not give out his phone number to friends, but that the regime has uncovered some of his other personal accounts that aren't so secure, such as his Xbox, FIFA video games, and Discord, as well as the accounts for some of his friends. It also mentions that his friends have low-security digital footprints and posts what appears to be screenshots of their profiles. It even names at least one of them. At some point, it apparently says, "This is just the beginning! Barron Trump, wait for us!" I debated whether or not to embed the video here, and I ultimately decided against it. Our managing editor Chris Queen suggested I link it for those who want to see it, and while it's not graphic, I will say that it's very disturbing, or, at least, it was to me. — it's easy to find on X as well if you're curious. Of course, this isn't the first time the Trump family has dealt with such threats from the regime. The president himself has been the target of several, as has the first lady, and some of Donald Trump's other children. There was even a "Where to Kill Melania" video circulating last month. "The U.S. Secret Service is aware of the video and investigates anything that can be perceived as a threat toward our protectees," a spokesperson for the Secret Service . "Out of concern for operational security, we do not discuss matters of protective intelligence." Experts say this is simply psychological warfare or propaganda, and there is likely no real immediate threat to Barron's life, although I have to say: I can be a little hot-headed at times, but if I had the power and this was my kid, I'd just have to finish them.
title: What the Iranian Regime Did to Barron Trump Will Make Your Blood Boil

movement_abstract: 伊朗国家电视台第三频道播放一段名为'在哪里杀死巴伦·特朗普'的三分钟视频，内容涉及对美国总统唐纳德·特朗普之子巴伦·特朗普的暗杀威胁。视频声称一名女子突破特勤局安保协议，获取了巴伦在纽约和华盛顿特区的日常生活、学校课程及出行路线等详细信息，并指出其特勤局特工伪装成学生混入校园。视频进一步声称发现巴伦在Xbox、FIFA游戏及Discord等数字平台存在安全漏洞，并展示其部分朋友的低安全数字足迹截图，甚至点名至少一名朋友。视频结尾宣称'这只是开始'，并暗示将实施行动。另有报道指该视频可能提供1000万美元悬赏，但尚未得到官方证实。美国特勤局发言人确认已注意到该视频，并表示正在调查任何可能构成威胁的情报，但出于行动安全考虑不讨论具体细节。专家分析认为此举属于心理战或宣传手段，目前暂无证据表明存在直接现实威胁。此前，特朗普家族其他成员也曾遭遇类似威胁视频。

movement_title: 台湾汉光演习强化军民整合动员应对中国威胁
movement_abstract: 【台湾联合新闻网报道】台湾防务部门近期结束年度汉光演习，演习范围扩展至资安、能源、交通、电信等民间领域，实现军政民跨界整合。演习不仅验证军事作战能力，更侧重战时社会韧性及民间基础设施持续运作能力，标志着汉光演习向全民防卫转型。国际媒体如《纽约时报》关注台湾民防运动发展，报道数千名普通民众参与民防训练，学习急救、疏散及人质营救技能。受中国灰色地带战术及军事胁迫影响，台湾涌现三十多个民间志愿团体，其中黑熊学院通过军事科普、资讯作战、卫生救护及避难规划等课程，提升公众防卫意志。国防安全研究院调查显示，71.6%民众愿意接受民防训练，主要兴趣集中在避难求生及自我保护技能。赖清德成立全社会防卫韧性委员会，旨在推动全民自我防护能力。演习与民防建设凸显台湾社会在应对地缘政治风险时的挑战与准备，强调维持日常生活及自救互救是对前线及社会的重要支持。

content: TEHRAN — President Donald Trump has turned to psychological warfare and media fabrications in a desperate attempt to distract from the failure of the US military and economic war against Iran. Such underhanded attempts became even more apparent after Trump reposted a link on Truth Social from the US conservative news outlet Newsmax, which grossly distorted comments made by Iran’s Parliament Speaker Mohammad Baqer Qalibaf during his recent diplomatic trip to Iraq. Newsmax sensationalized the story under the title "Iran Parliament Speaker: 'We Are Hungry, We Cannot Survive,'" attempting to cook up a false narrative of Iranian vulnerability by deliberately twisting Qalibaf’s words. Misquoting the Iranian Parliament speaker, the outlet wrote that no matter how strong military power becomes, if people are hungry, they will not be able to endure. Western outlets immediately spun the story to suggest that Iran is on the verge of collapse and that the US war against Iran, coupled with Washington’s unrelenting economic pressure, could bring down the Islamic Republic. Nonetheless, a look at Qalibaf’s actual speech delivered in Persian tells a completely different story and sheds light on what was truly said. In a high-level meeting with Iraqi and Iranian economic activists, Qalibaf spoke strategically about the vital need for sovereign nations to maintain both military and economic strength. In this section of his address, the Parliament speaker stressed that alongside formidable military power, economic growth, robust domestic production, and dynamic financial activity are essential pillars to maintaining a country’s overall strength and national resilience. He emphasized that military power alone cannot guarantee a country’s long-term survival if the domestic economy is neglected. In fact, Qalibaf firmly believes that alongside continuously strengthening its defense capabilities, Iran must also bolster its economic foundation and overcome its internal financial challenges precisely to withstand hostile foreign economic pressure. The media deception occurs against the backdrop of the aggressive US-Israeli war launched on February 28, a joint assault intended to cripple the Islamic Republic that ultimately backfired on its aggressors. When launching the operation, Trump openly declared an intent to force regime change, directly telling the Iranian population to take over their government. Yet, far from achieving its maximalist objectives or collapsing the government, the conflict resulted in the rapid depletion of the US military arsenal, exposing the logistical limits and strategic overreach of American hegemony. Detailed technical assessments and reports from major American military outlets confirm that months of high-intensity operations have severely drained US weapons stocks—expending nearly two-thirds of its Patriot air defense interceptor inventory, roughly 40 percent of its THAAD interceptors, and a third of its Tomahawk cruise missile supply, while virtually exhausting its precision strike ballistic missiles like ATACMS and PrSM. American military analysts have been forced to admit that Washington simply lacks the industrial manufacturing pace to replenish these advanced systems, proving that claims of having completely wiped out Iranian military power are detached from reality. Iranian military officials have repeatedly dismissed these US proclamations, noting that Iran's defense apparatus remains fully operational, integrated, and capable of sustained deterrence. Despite these clear tactical setbacks, Trump has continued to operate under extreme geopolitical delusions. Chief among them is his absurd, repeated assertion that the Strait of Hormuz—one of the world's most vital maritime choke points—is now sovereign American territory. Trump has publicly voiced this bizarre claim at least three times. He first floated the idea to a campaign crowd in Long Island, saying that after defeating Iran, he would declare the Strait a territory of the United States. He then doubled down during a press interaction at Joint Base Andrews, claiming the US possessed total control over the region and treated it as American ground. Shortly after, he amplified the delusion by sharing maps on Truth Social depicting the international waterway explicitly tagged as new US territory. Iranian officials and regional observers were quick to point out the unhinged nature of these statements. Officials in Tehran noted that the vast distance between Washington's military capability and its land-grab fantasies exposes the White House's complete detachment from realities on the ground. The Strait remains an international waterway bordered by sovereign nations, and no amount of Truth Social posts can grant Washington legal or physical ownership over foreign territorial waters. Trump's unfulfilled claims extend directly to his cycle of military threats, which have repeatedly collapsed into abrupt strategic retreats. This recurring pattern has become so glaring that analysts, financial markets, and international media outlets now widely refer to it as the TACO pattern, an acronym for "Trump Always Chickens Out". Time and again, Trump has issued dramatic ultimatums—threatening to bomb Iranian power plants, target critical energy infrastructure on Kharg Island, or send the country back to the Stone Age if his demands were not met within tight deadlines. Yet every single time the deadline expired and Tehran refused to submit, Trump backed away, offering unilateral extensions, claiming a deal was near, or citing requests from foreign leaders to pause military action. Having failed to secure a decisive victory on the battlefield, facing a depleted arsenal, and caught in a cycle of empty threats, Washington attempted to shift its focus back to financial strangulation. Trump orchestrated an "economic D-Day" plan against Iran—an aggressive economic warfare operation aimed at crushing the nation’s commercial lifelines and starving its people into submission. Yet, as Iran’s steadfast endurance neutralizes these hostile measures, Trump’s declared "economic D-Day" has crumbled into another total failure, exposing the utter limits of American coercive leverage. Facing structural defeat on both the military and financial fronts, the White House has resorted to a classic plan to divide and rule—using media fabrications, psychological manipulations on Truth Social, and false narratives about figures like Qalibaf to sow division and disguise Washington's growing impotence on the global stage.
title: Trump turns to smoke and mirrors
movement_title: 特朗普政府炮制伊朗经济崩溃假象掩盖军事行动失败
movement_abstract: 美国总统特朗普为掩盖对伊朗军事与经济战失败，利用社交媒体及保守派媒体Newsmax歪曲伊朗议长加利巴夫言论，炮制伊朗面临生存危机的虚假叙事。加利巴夫原意强调军事与经济双强对国家韧性的重要性，旨在应对外部压力。自2月28日美以联合军事行动以来，美军库存严重消耗，爱国者拦截弹消耗近三分之二，THAAD拦截弹消耗约40%，战斧巡航导弹消耗三分之一，精确打击弹道导弹几近耗尽，工业产能无法及时补充。特朗普多次宣称霍尔木兹海峡为美国领土，被伊朗及地区观察家驳斥。分析指出特朗普呈现“TACO”模式，即多次发出轰炸伊朗能源设施等最后通牒后均因未获屈服而退缩。其策划的“经济D日”封锁计划亦告失败。目前白宫转向心理战与媒体操纵，试图通过虚假信息掩盖战略无力。

author_name: By Dr. James Giordano and Dr. Robert Schmidle
content: Every competitive or conflictive human activity wields some form of power in attempt to affect . Diplomacy seeks to influence it through politics; economic sanctions seek to modify it through the distribution and access of goods; military operations seek to compel it through the threat or use of force; and information operations seek to shape it through exerting influence upon thought, attitudes, values and emotion. In all cases, whether acting upon policy makers, civilian populations, warfighters, and/or their commanders, all such strategic endeavors ultimately engage and operate through the human nervous system. Thus, the brain serves as the mediator of all enterprises of cooperation,or . Cognitive warfare certainly operates in and upon psychological and social dimensions of human action, but differs from historical forms of influence in the increasing ability to understand and exploit the neural substrates and mechanisms that contribute to, if not directly subserve thought, emotion, judgment, and . Contemporary neuroscience provides an iteratively expanding set of intelligence, surveillance and reconnaissance (ISR) data of the biological “terrain and conditions” in which cognitive warfare could be . We opine that the emergence of the brain-as-battlespace can be seen as a significant evolution in tactical nuance and strategic competition, as near future conflicts are likely to be defined and determined by who best employs such ISR to understand and influence the cognitive processes that shape human perception and action. Neuroscientific studies have demonstrated that cognition occurs through dynamic interactions among distributed, networked systems of the brain, which coordinate activity to continuously integrate internal and (for overview, see DiEuliis and Giordano). As schematically depicted in Figure 1, several neural systems are particularly relevant to cognitive warfare. Particularly, the salience network (which involves the anterior insula and anterior cingulate cortex) functions to identify information deemed important for survival and action. The default mode network supports self-referential thought, identity formation, memory integration, and narrative construction. Executive control networks (of the prefrontal cortex) are involved in planning, judgment, behavioral regulation, and decision-making; and limbic structures (e.g., the amygdala, hippocampus, and fornix) contribute to memory consolidation, threat detection, emotional processing, and affective learning, all of which evolved to support adaptive survival. : Diagrammatic representation of major functional networks in the human brain. Note that while defined aggregates of neural nodes and assemblies subtend types of cognitive functions and activities, there is some overlap of different networks’ involvement of brain structures and regions. Human cognition relies upon mental heuristics, biases, assumptions, and predictive mechanisms that frequently substitute accuracy for . These adaptive features can be targeted as exploitable vulnerabilities, and cognitive warfare seeks to identify these substrates and leverage such susceptibilities. One of the more influential models in contemporary neuroscience is predictive processing and coding theory, which establishes that the brain functions as an active prediction . Accordingly, the brain continuously generates representations of reality and compares incoming information against those expectations such that perception becomes an act of prediction. Thus, individuals actively filter incoming information according to dispositions formed by prior experiences, extant beliefs, emotions, expectations, and sociocultural frameworks. When incoming information confirms dispositional biases and expectations, cognitive “flow” is consonant and perceptions remain stable; when information conflicts with expectations, a condition of cognitive dissonance occurs, and existing schemas of reality must be modified, and/or incoming information (and decision trajectories) must be adapted. This reflects the well-known , and expands the construct to entails prior dispositions and biases, and the interpretive function of consequential effects of behavior (viz., a ; see Figure 2). This process is fundamental to understanding cognitive warfare. Effect(s) of biases (B) and consequences (C) on patterns of observation (O), orientation (O) contributory to neurocognitive processes of decision making (D) and resultant actions (A). neurocognitive processes of decision making (D) and resultant actions (A). Iterative experience(s) establish dispositional cognitions (i.e., biases) against which cognitive engagements of present factors are compared and appraised (via Bayesian dynamics) to influence initiation, extent and type of observation(s) and evaluative orientation(s). Relative valence of orienting processes as relevant to current factors, and reflective of prior value-based (cognitively biased) recollections (casuistically) inform and afford purchase to decisional options (that are weighted against prior experiential cognitions/memories, and their attendant emotional register) to (1) predict possible outcomes of different action effects and trajectories, and (2) compel action selection and execution. The (immediate and latent) consequences of action(s) are cognitively appraised relative to cognitive and emotional valences of prior experiences and actions. Consequences that are aligned with prior biases and expectations are positively reinforced, while those that are not prompt discordance. Additional details in text. Influence operations succeed because information (positively or negatively) interacts with pre-existing cognitive architectures. Narratives that align with existing beliefs (i.e., which are cognitively consonant) can propagate rapidly. Information that challenges core constructs, values and/or identities (i.e., which are cognitively dissonant) may be rejected regardless of objective accuracy. Thus, successful cognitive engagement depends upon (1) understanding how brains construct reality, and (2) by controlling the information itself. Trust determines whether information is accepted, rejected, amplified, or ignored, and thus one of the most important variables in cognitive warfare. Neuroscientific studies have demonstrated that feelings of trust occur through interactions of the brain’s mechanisms involved in social affiliation, group membership, cooperation, empathy, and collective . Humans exhibit strong tendencies toward in-group preference and out-group disfavor, and these tendencies may be amplified during periods of uncertainty, perceived threat, or social instability. Identity-based narratives, memes and semiotics exert influence because they engage these neural systems, and adversarial cognitive operations can exploit identity dynamics by targeting perceptions of belonging, legitimacy, victimization, grievance, and collective . The objective is to alter the social and emotional frameworks through which reality is interpreted, and in this way, affect individual and collective action. Neurocognitive processes can be targeted indirectly or . Most current cognitive warfare activities operate indirectly, by manipulating socio-environmental inputs via information ecosystems (e.g., digital media, social networks, algorithmic recommendation systems, news platforms, entertainment channels, and interpersonal communication) to influence neural processing to affect behavior “downrange.” Emotional content activates attentional systems; threat-related information engages defensive circuitry; social validation or disruption differentially activates reward networks; and narratives shape memory consolidation. With robust and/or repeated exposure, these effects accumulate such that beliefs become reinforced, attitudes become entrenched, and behavioral tendencies can become . This approach is a subtle, yet powerful feature of cognitive engagement, as it exploits natural neurocognitive mechanisms via indirect means that can be difficult to detect and directly attribute. Although indirect approaches to cognitive warfare are currently predominant, emerging technologies are increasingly enabling more direct assessment and potential modulation of neural activity. For example, advances in multimodal neuroimaging (e.g., convergent use of functional magnetic resonance imaging [fMRI], functional near infrared imaging [fNIR], magnetoencephalography [MEG], high-density quantitative electroencephalography [qEEG]) now afford ability for increasingly detailed observation, analyses and correlation of brain structure and functions. Brain-computer interfaces (BCIs) afford tools for sophisticated communication between neural systems and computational platforms, and neural decoding methods have made it possible to identify brain nodes and networks involved in perception, attention, intention, emotional state, and decision-making that could be targeted and modulated using ever more specific drugs, toxins, microbes, and devices (e.g., directable sonic and/or electromagnetic ). While limitations remain, these developments illustrate a notable trend toward increasing ability to assess, access and affect neurocognitive processes. Tactically and strategically, this affords capability for more diversified, and thus greater means of influence. The convergence of neuroscience, behavioral science, and computational analytics is transforming understanding and accessibility of human cognition at scale. Historically, neuroscientific research has focused upon individuals, with studies conducted in controlled environments. While valuable, these approaches can be inadequate for understanding how cognitive processes occur and manifest effect in large populations, and/or how collective behavior arises from individual . However, as we have , big data methods and technologies are affording capabilities to accumulate, assimilate, synthesize and analyze a huge amount of vastly different types and levels of information. Artificial intelligence systems can analyze big datasets to identify behavioral patterns, cognitive/emotional tendencies, preferences, vulnerabilities and volatilities, and do so in ways that enable individual-to-group and group-to-individual comparisons and norming. For example, machine learning systems are capable of integrating biological, psychological, social, cultural, economic, and informational variables simultaneously to identify patterns, correlations, and predictive relationships within datasets. The resulting capability is referred to as population . Population neuroanalytics enable improved understanding of neural, psychological, and behavioral processes at scale by identifying recurring patterns and relationships between neural mechanisms, psychological tendencies, social interactions, and collective action(s). While totally accurate (viz., “perfect”) prediction remains unrealistic, ever more sophisticated probabilistic models are now achievable. A next step beyond population neuroanalytics is development of synthetic cognitive modeling. Advances in computational neuroscience, agent-based modeling, machine learning, and digital-twin technologies are feasible for creating virtual representations of individuals, organizations, and populations. Of course, such models do not replicate actual brains, but instead afford simulacra of cognitive and behavioral tendencies based upon known relationships among neural, psychological, sociological, cultural, and environmental variables; the strategic utility of these systems is their ability to evaluate possible futures. Indubitably, all models possess limitations, and human behavior remains inherently complex, adaptive, and often unpredictable. Yet even imperfect predictive capability can afford significant strategic advantage, as synthetic cognitive environments may become indispensable tools for operational planning, deterrence and defense. To wit, synthetic cognitive modeling can provide valuable capabilities within the cognitive domain, given that such models may enable identification of several factors and functions, as summarized in Table 1. • Emerging social tensions • Declining institutional trust • Radicalization pathways • Information contagion dynamics • Social fragmentation indicators • Cognitive resilience factors • Decision-making vulnerabilities • Behavioral responses to crises In effect, the convergent use of big data techniques and tools, and AI enables far more nimble and thus functionally adaptive cognitive engagement, to instantiate a shift from mass persuasion toward precision influence. In this light, near future cognitive operations could be likened to precision-guided weaponry directed against specific targets rather than generalized assault. However, target specificity does not negate the viability or value of more broadly directed targeting. Indeed, the cognitive condition of populations can be a critical strategic variable and leveraging factor. Historically, the extrapolation of individual data to collective relevance has been difficult, given that no two brains are identical. Individuals differ genetically, developmentally, culturally, socially, and experientially. Moreover, collective behavior emerges through interactions among individuals rather than simple aggregation of individual traits. This complexity has limited attempts to extrapolate directly from neuroscience to population behavior. But the aforementioned scientific and technological developments are reducing, if not overcoming many of these impediments; and thus, the “brain-as-battlespace” of cognitive warfare is poised upon a cusp of capability. Throughout history, military power has depended upon understanding critical domains of engagement and effect. To be sure, the aforementioned convergence of neuroscience, big data, AI, biotechnology, and information technology creates a new engagement environment that we believe could be regarded as the milieu of neurocognitive strategic competition. Currently, states that successfully integrate these disciplines could acquire unprecedented capabilities to understand and shape human thought and behavior. The implications extend beyond military operations. Political stability, economic confidence, social cohesion, and national resilience all depend upon such cognitive factors. Accordingly, we argue that cognitive security must become a central component of national security. To remain apace of, if not preferably ahead of peer-competitors’ and adversarial developments, we advocate that the DoW should establish an interdisciplinary and operationally focused . Toward such an enterprise, the following lines of effort are proposed: 1. , to develop methods and improved tools to assess cognitive vulnerabilities and resilience across military forces, governmental institutions, and critical populations. 2. , toward advancing understanding of relationships among neural architectures and mechanisms, cognitive processes, behavioral dynamics, social cohesion, and strategic stability. 3. to create systems capable of monitoring evolving cognitive and emotional trends that are relevant to national security. 4. to develop technologies that enhance decision-making while preserving human judgment and ethical oversight. 5. aimed at identifying methods to strengthen resistance against manipulation, misinformation, coercion, and adversarial influence. 6. to monitor global developments in neuroscience, neurotechnology, AI-enabled behavioral systems, and related dual-use capabilities. 7. to develop rigorous methodologies for measuring cognitive effects and evaluating operational outcomes. 8. ensuring responsible development and use of cognitive-security capabilities. Toward achieving these ends, we offer the following recommendations: 1. The DoW should establish a permanent cross-functional organization integrating expertise from neuroscience, behavioral science, biotechnology, AI, strategic deterrence, and military planning. 2. A dedicated intelligence effort should continuously monitor foreign developments in neurotechnology, computational neuroscience, cognitive warfare, AI-enabled behavioral analytics, and related dual-use capabilities. Particular attention should focus upon activities conducted by China, Russia, Iran, and North Korea. 3. The Department should establish secure infrastructures capable of integrating behavioral, informational, sociological, and neurocognitive datasets while maintaining appropriate legal and ethical safeguards. Such architectures will be essential for future cognitive-security operations and analyses. 4. Training, education, leader development, and force-preparation programs should incorporate cognitive-security principles. The objective should be development of cognitively resilient personnel, organizations, and populations capable of recognizing and resisting adversarial influence efforts. 5. Long-term investment is required. Short funding cycles are insufficient for sustained advancement in neuroscience and technology, big data, and AI. A dedicated research portfolio should be established comparable to historical investments in nuclear deterrence, cyber security, and biodefense. The future of strategic competition will be defined and determined by the ability to understand, influence, protect, and defend the human cognitive processes that shape perception, judgment, decision-making, and behavior. Advances in neuroscience are revealing the neural substrates that are involved in and subserve thought, emotion, and action. Concomitant advances in big data and AI are enabling unprecedented capacity to examine relationships between individual cognition and collective behavior. Taken together, these developments have established cognition as a domain of tactical accessibility, strategic relevance and operational viability and value. Adversaries recognize this reality and are actively pursuing capabilities designed to exploit cognitive vulnerabilities, manipulate perceptions, degrade trust, and influence thought, emotion and . The U.S. cannot afford to regard such developments as merely academic or theoretical but instead should acknowledge and respond to such advancements as emerging risks and threats to national security. Thus, the challenge and opportunity for DoW is to strengthen the scientific, technological, operational, and ethical foundations necessary to successfully secure and protect the neurocognitive domain. Indubitably, success of an enterprise of this magnitude will necessitate sustained investment, interdisciplinary collaboration, strategic foresight, and whole-of-nation . As previous generations developed doctrines for nuclear deterrence, and biological and chemical weapons governance and control, we opine that it is now vital to develop a coherent doctrine of cognitive security and neurostrategic competition. For in this emerging environment, strategic advantage will increasingly belong to those who most effectively understand and protect the biological, psychological and social dimensions that influence human thought, emotion, judgment, and action. The views and opinions expressed in this essay are those of the authors and do not necessarily reflect those of the United States government, Department of War, or the National Defense University. Dr. James Giordano is Head of the Center for Strategic Deterrence and Study of Weapons of Mass Destruction, and Program Lead for Disruptive Technology and Future Warfare of the Institute for National Strategic Studies at the National Defense University. He is also Professor Emeritus of Neurology, Biochemistry, and Ethics at Georgetown University Medical Center. Dr. Robert Schmidle (LtGen, USMC, ret) is a Professor of Professional Practice in the Irregular Warfare Center at the Arizona State University.

movement_abstract: 【美国国防大学国家战略研究所2026年8月报道】美国国防大学国家战略研究所詹姆斯·吉奥尔达诺博士与罗伯特·施米德尔博士发表文章，提出将认知安全确立为国家安全核心组成部分。文章指出，随着神经科学、大数据与人工智能的融合，'大脑即战场'已成为战略竞争新领域。对手正利用神经机制漏洞操纵感知、情绪与决策，威胁政治稳定与社会凝聚力。文章建议美国国防部（DoW）建立跨学科认知安全机构，整合神经科学、行为科学及AI技术。具体举措包括：开发认知脆弱性评估工具、建立全球神经技术监测机制、构建安全数据基础设施、加强人员认知韧性训练及设立长期研发基金。文章特别强调需重点关注中国、俄罗斯、伊朗及朝鲜在神经技术与认知战领域的进展。作者主张制定认知安全与神经战略竞争学说，通过精准影响替代大规模说服，以保护国家神经认知领域安全。
